meeting_header:
Date: 2025-11-06
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Kapoor (Redwood AE); Marco Diaz (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Jacob Lin (Novus - Procurement); Priya Sharma (Novus - Legal); Ethan Cole (Novus - CISO); Marta Velez (Novus - Eng); Samir Patel (Novus - Finance)
Recording: Yes (auto-transcript)
summary: Procurement-led call to review MSA/DPA, confirm security requirements (SOC2, encryption, audit logs), and align on pricing approval and onboarding timeline. Redwood agreed to send redlined contracts, security package, and committed pricing proposal. Technical deep-dive with Novus security/engineering to be scheduled next week; pilot kickoff targeted mid-November.
transcript:
00:00 - Aisha: hey everyone thanks for joining on a friday afternoon, appreciate it. we can do quick intros and then jump into the MSA/DPA items.
00:18 - Jacob: thanks aisha, this is Jacob from procurement, I'll be leading the contract side here. we have Priya from legal, Ethan our CISO, Marta from eng and Samir from finance here.
00:30 - Aisha: perfect, i will hand to marco for a 2 minute overview of what's in the security package and what you can expect in the docs.
00:40 - Marco: yeah hi all, Marco Diaz, senior solutions engineer at Redwood. quick high level: MSA is our standard terms, DPA covers data processing — we also include SOC 2 type two, pen test summary, architecture diagram, encryption at rest and in transit, support SLAs and optional dedicated/private deployment clauses. i'm going to call out a few things that typically come up: KMS integration options, audit logs retention, and regional data residency.
01:05 - Priya: thanks, that helps. Jacob — we forwarded a couple of redline flags earlier but wanted to talk through liabilities and indemnities and also the subprocessor list.
01:20 - Aisha: yep, those are important. our legal team usually accepts most procurement redlines but we often propose alternative language on liability caps and breach notification windows. we'll send a redline back.
01:35 - Ethan: quick security note — we need to confirm whether customer-managed keys (KMS) are supported in your hosted offering or if that's only for Private/VPC. we also want clarification on log forwarding to our SIEM and retention.
01:50 - Marco: good question. KMS is available in Private deployments and in Dedicated with KMS integration; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in some regions — i will confirm the list. log forwarding we can stream via syslog or S3 and we have configurable retention and export hooks.
02:15 - Marta: for the pilot we will run some load tests — can you share rough throughput per GPU profile and latency percentiles? This will help us size the pilot.
02:30 - Marco: yes, i'll attach a pilot runbook and sample benchmark spreadsheet — expect p50/p95 numbers depending on model and batch config, but we'll share examples that mirror small-realtime workloads.
02:45 - Samir: on pricing — we need committed capacity proposals and a blended per-token or per-instance rate for budgeting. what's the timeline to get pricing for procurement approval?
02:58 - Aisha: we'll send a committed pricing worksheet and a couple of example TCV scenarios by Monday. typical lead time for procurement review is two weeks once you have the TCV.
03:12 - Jacob: ok good. Priya, any immediate redlines?
03:20 - Priya: mainly the indemnity language, data processing liability, and a clause about audit rights and subprocessor notifications. also we'd like more explicit SLA uptime numbers and credits in the MSA.
03:33 - Aisha: understandable. our standard SLA is 99.9% for hosted endpoints and higher SLAs for Dedicated with reserved capacity — we can map that in the MSA and define credit mechanisms.
03:47 - Ethan: also need to confirm breach notification window — 72 hours acceptable? and will you provide an incident response liaison?
03:58 - Lena: yes, we provide incident contact and typically 72 hours is in line with our practice; we'll include escalation contacts in the security package.
04:10 - Jacob: great. any redlines to pricing on committed terms?
04:20 - Samir: we prefer annual committed capacity with predictable unit pricing; any termination or true-up rules we should know about?
04:30 - Aisha: termination for convenience vs for cause — we can discuss options. for committed capacity we include true-up periods and options to change capacity at renewal. we'll include a sample schedule.
04:45 - Marco: i'll note the need to include burst and overage pricing examples in the workbook.
05:00 - Marta: technical — for the pilot we'll need a VPC option and control plane access patterns. is the private deployment on-prem or VPC in a public cloud?
05:15 - Marco: Private can be VPC-hosted in your cloud or on-prem. for Novus pilot we usually recommend Dedicated in your VPC to get predictable throughput with less ops overhead — we can outline both options.
05:30 - Ethan: if we do VPC, we need to validate network egress controls and our firewall rules. can you provide a minimal set of IP ranges and ports?
05:45 - Marco: yes, we will provide an allow-list and more detailed network diagram in the runbook.
06:00 - Jacob: timeline check — procurement target is sign-off by end of November if possible. are we confident on that cadence?
06:12 - Aisha: yes that's aligned — if we get redlines and the security packet next week and your team returns comments, end of November is achievable.
06:25 - Priya: ok we'll aim to return redlines within a week.
06:30 - Marco: quick note on data residency — if you need EU-only storage we have region pinning in Dedicated and Private; hosted may have options depending on region.
06:45 - Marta: also curious about model custody and logs: will you retain prompts or will there be an option to not persist PII?
06:55 - Marco: default retention is short and we have options to disable retention for specific routes; DPA will outline retention terms. if you need stronger controls we typically recommend Dedicated or Private.
07:10 - Samir: what about audit logs for usage and walleting? we need token-level billing to reconcile costs.
07:20 - Lena: our console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and you can export that to CSV or BI. We'll include a sample export in the packet.
07:35 - Jacob: sounds good. any blockers from Redwood to provide SOC 2 evidence?
07:42 - Marco: none — we'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and a recent pen test summary; some items are redacted but it's standard.
07:55 - Priya: moving on — indemnity cap language: we usually expect mutual indemnity except in cases of willful misconduct. what's your standard?
08:10 - Aisha: standard is mutual with a financial cap tied to fees paid in the preceding year; however for privacy breaches we have alternate language, happy to propose options.
08:22 - Ethan: regarding encryption, is HSM-backed key storage supported — we need FIPS-compliant keys for some workloads.
08:32 - Marco: we support customer-managed keys with HSM in Dedicated and Private; for hosted we can discuss managed CMKs in supported clouds — i'll confirm the compliance posture.
08:45 - Marta: for the pilot test cases — we will run 3 prompt sets including PII redaction scenarios; we may need a dedicated endpoint to avoid cold-cache interference.
08:58 - Marco: yes for isolated tests we recommend pinned model versions and a dedicated route; we'll show how to pin and run canary deployments.
09:10 - Samir: finance question — are there any implementation fees or setup fees for Dedicated or Private?
09:20 - Aisha: there can be an initial onboarding fee for Private deployments and dedicated capacity setup — we'll include a breakdown in the pricing sheet and highlight optional vs included items.
09:33 - Jacob: ok. Priya, any compliance questions for the DPA?
09:40 - Priya: subprocessor notification cadence — we want notice within 30 days for new subprocessors, and the right to object. is that in your DPA?
09:50 - Marco: standard is notification, and we have procedures to respond to objections; i'll surface the current subprocessors list and the notification cadence.
10:05 - Aisha: let's talk about SLAs more concretely. hosted 99.9% is our baseline, Dedicated can be 99.95% with reserved pools. we can include P95 latency targets for a given model class in the SLO appendix.
10:25 - Ethan: and credits — how is the credit calculated? is it a percentage of monthly fees?
10:32 - Lena: typically a tiered credit based on downtime percentage; we'll share the exact table in the MSA exhibit.
10:45 - Priya: also want to add a clause for regulatory audits — if Novus needs to audit the security controls will Redwood accommodate on-site or virtual audits?
10:58 - Marco: we support virtual audits and provide documentation; on-site audits for hosted offerings are rare but possible for Private deployments.
11:12 - Jacob: logistics — when you send the redlines, can you include a 'what changed' summary so our legal can quickly triage?
11:20 - Aisha: yes we'll include a summary and call out any high-risk clauses.
11:28 - Samir: regarding billing cycles — monthly in arrears or prepaid? we typically prefer monthly but can do prepaid for discounts.
11:38 - Aisha: both supported; prepaid gives better discounts and easier forecasting. we'll include examples in the pricing workbook.
11:48 - Marta: one technical ask — will Redwood support our SSO (SAML) and SCIM for user provisioning in the console?
12:00 - Marco: yes, SSO/SAML and SCIM are supported; we'll include the SSO metadata and SCIM endpoints in the packet.
12:12 - Priya: on DPA termination — need clear data deletion on termination and certificate of deletion. is that available?
12:22 - Marco: yes, we provide data deletion processes and can provide certification for deletion for Private/Dedicated; we'll confirm hosted options.
12:35 - Jacob: next steps recap would be helpful.
12:40 - Aisha: agreed — i'll recap and then we'll open to any final q's.
12:45 - Priya: one last question — do you have a model for escrow of data if vendor insolvency occurs?
12:55 - Aisha: we can discuss third-party escrow options; it's not common but doable for enterprise deals, we'll flag it to legal.
13:10 - Marta: timeline again — if we get all items this week we'll aim for legal signoff by 11/28; that works on our side.
13:22 - Aisha: great. recap of actions: i'll send redlined MSA/DPA, Marco will send runbook/benchmarks and subprocessors, lena will send onboarding checklist and SLA exhibit, and we'll propose pricing by Monday.
13:40 - Jacob: excellent — we'll look to return redlines and set the technical deep-dive. thanks everyone.
13:50 - Aisha: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites for the tech deep-dive. bye.
14:00 - [meeting ends]
